objective: triển khai các đề xuất để tối ưu

phaseOneRelease.verification: 18 original targets match phase-one source; the remaining five match the consolidated b9 source. See per-function evidence in the verification record.

D0.0.finding: Bounded renewal logs classified 52 HTTP 500 and 13 HTTP 429 at 17:05 UTC as no available platform instance. This does not classify earlier errors of other services.
D0.0.currentHealth: Three inspected services have healthy current serving revisions at 100 percent traffic. Retry subscriptions are ACTIVE; backlog and oldest unacked age were observed as zero through 18:06 UTC. No runtime scale change in this release.

D0.1.change: Valid queue path, transactional enqueue dedupe, generation guarded completion/failure, real stale reader to worker integration.

D0.2.change: Complete paginated inventory before planning; re-read changed cases and dependencies transactionally; closed Sales cases and fresh user fields preserved; bounded writer concurrency.
D0.2.remaining: Full inventory scans remain until D4.4 due queue replaces them.

D0.3.change: Seven complete Vietnam calendar days of scoped Monitoring metrics and Billing/export metadata recorded in ops/data-cost-seven-day-baseline-20261025.json. Seven Enterprise query plans and the READY ledger date index are recorded separately.
D0.3.remaining: Currency/provider attribution, a clean post-release baseline, representative runtime metrics and remaining query inventory. Historical request attempts include retries and deployment/repair activity; API method aliases must not be summed.

D1.1.change: Finance directories attach only while detail consumers are mounted; StrictMode and repeated cleanup tested.

D1.2.change: Foreground/online guards, single-flight reads, stale response fencing, stop terminal order polling, selection-independent load and driver mutation patches. Dispatch config drafts survive background reads.
D1.2.remaining: Dispatcher and per-order tracking still need their authorized event/state/location split in D2.3.

D1.3.change: Stable weight, body and check-in subscriptions; photos only in body/history with shared lifecycle.
D1.3.remaining: Photo cursor and daily chart summaries are later data model work.

D1.4.change: Session notes/metadata skip Action Center reads; reassignment reconciles both students and leaves unrelated alerts intact.

D1.5.change: Unchanged wizard prepare preserves revision/updateTime while rereading current authority and sales/payment options.

D1.6.change: Transaction compares mission business payload before writing. Duplicate concurrent mission writes collapse; progress-only changes persist.
D1.6.remaining: One comparison read per mission is added; assess billed-unit tradeoff. Historical contribution/source-watermark redesign remains D4.5.

D2.1.change: Availability uses existing account-scoped schedule revisions, retains pending changes while editing, refreshes at Vietnam midnight without losing drafts, and fences reads/saves by account/week. Availability-only response skips session-request history and trainer-name reads while preserving booked slots, contracts and leave periods.
D2.1.validation: 40 backend scope/signal tests; 7 sync-controller tests; browser idle/draft/save/account/revocation/day-boundary checks. At 2026-10-24T18:54:32Z all 11 current serving signal producers were verified from their exact image digests: reviewed signal module hash and source-trigger wiring matched.
D2.1.remaining: Representative post-release read-unit, latency and error measurement.

D2.2.change: Separate plan/history revisions on existing account metadata. Personal plan reads stop periodic polling; inactive tabs retain invalidations. History is fetched only on opening, with 25-row cursor pages, 26-row maximum query and scope/version validation. Statistics explicitly cover loaded rows. Account changes remount personal state; refresh supersedes in-flight append. New plan-only source trigger never rebuilds scheduling or Student 360.
D2.2.validation: 32 backend signal/workout tests; 33 Chromium and 33 mobile Safari workspace browser checks including 7 new personal workout cases per browser; 4 real Firestore read-budget, cursor and authorization checks; full npm run ci passed.
D2.2.remaining: Real usage and billing observation, including source-trigger deliveries and metadata maintenance.

D2.3.change: The driver workspace replaces its 30-second full-list timer with current-role-protected, metadata-only revisions. Four source triggers cover orders, deliveries, shipper availability and shared configuration. Commit-time watermarks skip duplicate/older writes and address old/new assignees independently. The authorized reader acknowledges two marker documents before hydration; initial snapshots catch bootstrap races. Hidden/offline changes remain pending, bursts coalesce, local mutations fence older responses, and an explicit own-account listener clears cached jobs after access changes. SLA deadlines reuse the existing local alarm hook, updating labels and resuming after suspension without network reads.
D2.3.validation: Eight backend integration/registration checks and all 45 Firestore rule checks passed. Twenty-four delivery browser cases passed across Chromium and mobile Safari, including 30 idle foreground minutes without another list request, 30-event bursts, bootstrap/in-flight races, old-account reads/mutations, hidden/offline resume, access revocation, scope changes, bounded error recovery and local SLA deadlines. Two existing student-schedule deadline cases also passed after extracting the shared clock hook unchanged. The earlier regression browser run passed 24 checks (nine delivery cases plus 15 existing listener/GPS/history-isolation cases). Full local npm run ci passed before the clock follow-up; typecheck, build/performance and focused browser checks validate that follow-up. All nine source CI checks and CodeQL passed. The release workflow passed, all five serving images matched reviewed source, all four event filter/transport bindings matched, and the public frontend passed smoke after merge.
D2.3.readBudget: Each driver list request adds two metadata document reads before existing authorized business reads. Each source event touches at most four small marker documents; order events add one current-delivery lookup for legacy/current ownership. Replays can read markers but do not rewrite them. Metadata-only order/config edits skip database work. Delivery updatedAt remains significant because it changes query ordering. GPS stays in RTDB and does not publish these signals.
D2.3.releaseOrder: Verified the four event handlers, additive listMyShipperJobs response and Firestore rules before merging PR17. Public frontend smoke verified the merge SHA. Missing markers bootstrap at zero; no production business records or GPS points were synthesized.
D2.3.remaining: Dispatcher and per-order location surfaces still have their existing guarded 30/15-second polling. Their independent state/count/config/GPS streams, authorized location transport and complete page UX remain follow-ups. This completes only the driver-screen portion after production verification. Measure added event/marker/profile-listener costs against avoided full-list reads; no billing reduction percentage is claimed.

D2.4.change: Shared GPS policy: hard 15-second attempt/write interval, 60-second stationary refresh using fresh fixes only, 30-second sample age, 100m maximum uncertainty and implausible-jump rejection. Retain only the newest point, stop on account/job/readiness changes or terminal authorization errors. RTDB transaction arbitrates concurrent devices and preserves newer inactive/reassigned mirrors without writing Firestore.
D2.4.validation: 5 request-budget/quality/controller tests, 5 actual hook browser lifecycle tests, 5 real RTDB emulator transaction/authorization tests, 28 existing Eat Clean tests and TypeScript passed.
D2.4.remaining: Real-route freshness and accuracy observation. No direct browser RTDB permissions were added.

D2.5.change: The trainer's own attendance mutations pause source-driven refreshes while saving and route post-response reconciliation through the same signal engine. Thirty in-flight bulk source signals coalesce once after success. Late source versions still reconcile, hidden/offline state retains pending work, and operation identity fences old week/account responses and cleanup.
D2.5.validation: Chromium/mobile Safari coverage for 30-signal bulk writes, late markers, partial success, hidden resume, failed requests, week changes and overlapping account operations; TypeScript. Hosted CI and scoped production serving verification passed; see productionVerification.
D2.5.remaining: This reduces reads on the submitting trainer screen only. Other viewers still observe per-source events. Shared mutation receipts/accepted source versions and backend batching need a separate change; reading the marker after a mutation cannot safely prove which unrelated changes its patch covers.

D3.2.change: Finance entry-only workspace explicitly skips the unused all-period summary. History cursor pages retain first-page totals within the same person/filter scope. Complete-day canonical paging now keeps ISO-date and mirror rows together, advances through empty filtered windows, and binds new cursors to the current authorized subject/filter scope. Status filtering follows canonicalization so records and totals agree. An exhausted first range reuses its source rows for totals; legacy cursors remain accepted.
D3.2.validation: 24 history behavior/access/read-budget checks; five real Firestore scenarios; 14 Chromium/mobile Safari history panel checks; full local npm run ci. Earlier finance and summary validations remain applicable. Hosted CI and scoped production serving verification passed; see productionVerification.
D3.2.readBudget: At most four page queries: first pageSize*3+1, at most 301 rows for each later query. A single incomplete day beyond this budget raises a non-retryable data precondition, preventing automatic cross-region rescans. Summary and authorization reads have separate existing budgets. Within-day trainer cursors reread that day to select complete canonical slots.
D3.2.tradeoff: Removing the premature status predicate fixes cancelled-mirror inconsistencies but can scan more source rows for sparse status filters. No read-unit or currency saving is claimed for that correction; use a canonical projection if measured demand justifies its maintenance cost.
D3.2.remaining: Finance directory cursors and per-operation billed-unit observation.

D3.6.change: Dashboard cache misses coordinate across instances through a 60-second transactional lease. Followers wait at most eight seconds, reuse the published result, and never independently hydrate the same cold scope. Forced refresh supersedes older builders; expired or superseded tokens cannot publish or populate process memory. Retention expiry is separate from payload freshness, under a new cache schema/key.
D3.6.validation: 36 dashboard unit/read-budget tests; five real Firestore scenarios for simultaneous cold misses, force-refresh fencing, crashed worker takeover, retention/freshness separation and bounded waiting. Existing actor/permission/branch cache isolation is retained.
D3.6.remaining: Detail cursors, source-domain revisions and narrower contracts/students aggregates remain separate follow-ups. Measure lease read/write overhead against duplicate cold builds under representative traffic; a crashed builder can delay the next build for up to 60 seconds.

D3.5.change: The Progress overview reads existing nutrition daily summaries in 31-day windows, replacing three recent raw-history listeners. Schema v2 records main meal occasions and distinct snack times so multiple dishes do not inflate adherence. Type/time edits, moved dates and deletes rebuild affected days. Hidden/offline screens defer work, finished chunks survive a pause, and body/history tabs reuse the completed report. Pending, incomplete or old-schema data never produces a percentage; bounded cold builds resume only on explicit request. Owner/range changes fence previous responses.
D3.5.validation: Full local npm run ci; 10 daily-summary unit tests; six nutrition progress tests; seven real Firestore scenarios, including 1800 meal logs over 90 days, schema upgrade, move/delete and meal-type/time edits. Warm 90-day reads use 90 daily documents with no raw source query or summary write, excluding authorization. Browser tests cover idle reads, mobile viewport, partial/error states, explicit continuation, visibility/offline and owner/range races. Hosted CI and scoped production serving verification passed; see productionVerification.
D3.5.releaseOrder: Deploy and verify syncNutritionMealDailySummary, syncNutritionWaterDailySummary, syncNutritionActivityDailySummary and getMyNutritionJournalSummary before the new frontend. Existing calendar readers accept the additive response. No new listener, collection or callable is introduced.
D3.5.tradeoff: Existing v1 summaries rebuild lazily once per requested day. Source-trigger maintenance and an explicit forced reconciliation still read raw source rows within existing request/day/time budgets. Report data stays fixed while the same day/range remains open until manual refresh or a new scope; this is not a live diary. No production cost saving percentage is claimed.
D3.5.remaining: Photo/check-in cursors, other historical chart consumers and representative production read-unit observation.

D4.1.change: Warm Student 360 progress events read only the six existing progress sources, with the same newest-first limits and canonical mirror handling as a full rebuild. Progress, nutrition and full refreshes share one fenced lease but keep independent coverage watermarks. Profile/account versions are rechecked transactionally before publishing. Photo-only changes can update the timeline without rewriting the overview; unchanged progress payloads avoid metadata-only overview writes.
D4.1.validation: Full local npm run ci passed. Nine real Firestore progress scenarios cover a fixture with over 1000 sessions and attendance rows, same-commit mirrors, edits/backdating/deletes/restoration, stale bases, full/nutrition races, later source writes, profile/account changes, legacy account resolution, photo-only writes and the 300-document source ceiling. Twelve existing nutrition/refresh-queue integration scenarios also passed, alongside 13 projection-write tests. Hosted CI and scoped production serving verification passed; see productionVerification.
D4.1.readBudget: A warm progress refresh makes six bounded source queries, at most 300 source documents total, plus owner/projection/profile/lease reads and timeline comparison transactions. It does not query sessions, attendance, contracts, finance, meals or workout history. Existing full-rebuild source limits are unchanged.
D4.1.releaseOrder: The six progress triggers and generateAuraContent were released together in run 40139824732; exact serving images and event transports passed before PR15 merge and public smoke.
D4.1.tradeoff: Missing, stale, incomplete or legacy/changed-account bases use the full repair path. Full freshness is not advanced by a progress-only update. Existing timeline retention is preserved. Normal student/staff check-in writers batch subcollection mirrors without rewriting the root user profile; independent profile edits still require full recomputation.
D4.1.remaining: Representative billed-unit/latency observation; schedule, contract, finance and training domains; durable dirty masks, ownership move reconciliation and historical timeline lifecycle.

D4.2.change: Student, trainer and contract deliveries that only touch root updatedAt stop before weekly-view target discovery, avoiding historical-view reads, dirty-generation writes and rebuilds. Every other source field remains significant; creates/deletes, nested timestamps, ownership moves and backdated edits still propagate. The existing contract-usage verification guard is retained.
D4.2.validation: 52 weekly/source unit tests and 14 real Firestore scenarios passed, including zero database work for metadata-only events and continued invalidation of historical, moved and cross-branch scopes. Functions syntax checks, repository hygiene and secret scan passed. Hosted CI and scoped production serving verification passed; see productionVerification.
D4.2.remaining: No event invocation savings are claimed. Replayed business events still increment generations; per-target durable receipts and narrower dependency fingerprints require separate work. Existing historical scope is preserved.

D5.constraint: Endpoint retirement still requires lifecycle evidence and observation windows; no automatic deletion at the earliest dates.

D5.1.change: generateAuraContent permits one model fallback only for a narrow explicit HTTP 400/404 model or format rejection without generation identifiers, usage or choices. Network/body failures, timeouts, rate limits, gateway errors and incomplete, malformed or empty generations return their error without a second application POST. Auth, App Check, rate limits, primary/fallback configuration, success schema and usage metadata are preserved.
D5.1.validation: Full local npm run ci passed. 22 content/router tests passed, including actual content request wiring, synthetic provider failures, generation evidence, two-attempt ceiling, successful usage metadata and the existing shared-router behavior. No paid provider requests were used. Hosted CI and scoped production serving verification passed; see productionVerification.
D5.1.releaseOrder: generateAuraContent was included in the same seven-function release as the progress triggers. Source/serving health was verified; no paid provider request was made.
D5.1.tradeoff: An ambiguous provider failure is surfaced instead of automatically trying another model. This bounds application-level automatic attempts; it does not constrain provider-internal routing, prove whether an attempt was charged, or deduplicate separate user requests.
D5.1.remaining: Durable owner/request receipts, payload/version hashes, pending/succeeded/unknown recovery and explicit new-draft semantics across reloads and instances. The original Academy editing work remains excluded.

D5.5.change: One ordered ledger date index was created and verified READY. Unfiltered descending ledger pages now use a date-range SequentialScan without MajorSort. Existing 92 indexes were preserved; branch/history indexes were reused. Evidence: ops/ledger-date-index-observation-20261025.json. Six collection-scoped date/document-ID descending indexes are now READY for progress sources. All six synthetic explain plans use ordered SequentialScan without TableScan or MajorSort. Existing 93 indexes were preserved; total 99. Evidence: ops/progress-date-index-observation-20261025.json.
D5.5.remaining: Measure runtime and read benefit against added index write/storage overhead; other retention/index work remains pending. Ascending report plans still sort.
D5.5.validation: Seven index-scope/target/direction tests passed; create-only apply verified six created, six READY and zero deleted; independent dry-run verified 99 indexes and no missing progress target. Regional routing/lifecycle regression checks are recorded with this change.
